message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze this situation carefully.

The user's position: Aave V3 Ethereum Core, supplies WETH (~$1,000), no debt. So the user is a supplier/lender of WETH.

Timeline of events:
1. 17:30 - Normal-ish: WETH utilization 88.6%, rsETH adapter balance unchanged.
2. 17:35 - Kelp rsETH OFTAdapter released 116,500 rsETH (~$292M) in one LayerZero delivery — this is the exploit. Adapter balance dropped 99.8%.
3. 17:37 - Aave official says "scheduled treasury rebalance, no reserve deficit, keep deposits" — this appears to be a false/misleading statement (possibly spoofed or premature). Actually wait, this is labeled official_x from "Aave V3 Ethereum Core official team". Hmm, but later Aave official confirms exploit. The 17:37 message seems to be downplaying. Interesting — could be a fake account, but we take observations at face value; regardless, later evidence contradicts it.
4. 17:38-17:44 - Fresh address supplied 52,999 rsETH (stolen) and borrowed 52,439.6 WETH (~$236M?) in e-mode near max LTV, taking WETH out as ETH. WETH utilization rose to 90.3%.
5. 18:21 - Kelp paused rsETH token and related contracts.
6. 18:44 - BWEnews: Aave v3 suffering bad debt due to KelpDAO hack.
7. 19:03 - Aave froze rsETH reserve.
8. 19:17-19:20 - PeckShield, The Block confirm ~$292M exploit of rsETH bridge.
9. 19:20 - $535M USDT withdrawn from Aave; USDT utilization to 89.8%.
10. 19:21 - Marc Zeller: "If you have WETH on Aave V3 Core, withdraw now, ask questions later."
11. 19:36 - 231,870 WETH withdrawn in 15 min; WETH utilization 97.33%, idle 75k.
12. 19:45 - WETH utilization 99.0%, idle 25,585 WETH.
13. 19:55 - Aave official: rsETH markets frozen; Aave contracts not exploited; exploit related to rsETH.
14. 20:05 - WETH utilization 99.7%, idle WETH 13 WETH (!). Essentially no liquidity left for withdrawals. Borrow rate 8.35%.
15. 20:08 - Stani: rsETH frozen, no borrowing power, Aave has no further exposure to rsETH.
16. 20:10 - Kelp confirms suspicious activity, paused contracts.
17. 20:13 - Cyvers: $293M drained.
18. 20:29 - PeckShield: exploiter deposited stolen rsETH into AaveV3, CompoundV3, Euler and borrowed massive WETHs with >$236M debt.
19. 20:36 - BeInCrypto: Aave WETH suppliers urged to withdraw; WETH reserve carrying bad debt; partial withdrawals may only be possible after Umbrella backstop settles deficit.

Key question: risk to a WETH supplier with no debt on Aave V3 Core.

The attacker borrowed ~52,439.6 WETH (~$236M at ~$4,500/ETH? Actually 52,439 WETH... if $236M debt total, ETH ~ $4,500). The collateral is stolen rsETH which is now worthless/frozen. So Aave V3 Core WETH pool has uncollateralized debt of ~$236M (the borrowed WETH is bad debt). WETH suppliers bear this loss — the pool's supplies back the borrows. With ~3M WETH supply (~$13.5B?), wait idle was 342k WETH earlier, supply 3.008M WETH. Bad debt of ~52,439 WETH against 3M WETH supply is ~1.7% loss. Hmm, but wait — actually the attacker borrowed 52,439.6 WETH. That's the bad debt if rsETH collateral is worthless. Actually rsETH collateral was 52,999 rsETH. rsETH price ~$4,500? 52,999 rsETH ≈ $238M. So borrowed 52,439 WETH ≈ $236M. If rsETH is worthless (bridge drained, token paused, frozen), the WETH borrowed is bad debt borne by WETH suppliers.

Also, Umbrella (Aave's safety module) will socialize/backstop the deficit, but that may involve slashing aTokens or the backstop covering. The BeInCrypto article says partial withdrawals may only become possible after Umbrella settles the deficit.

Meanwhile, WETH utilization is ~100%, idle WETH is 13 WETH. So withdrawals cannot be processed right now — there's no liquidity. The user cannot actually withdraw; any exit attempt would fail or be partial. But the action we propose is what the keeper should do. If liquidity is zero, exit attempts will revert. Hmm.

But wait — the position is only $1,000 WETH. The keeper can only propose an action; corridor limits enforce safety. The realistic options:

- exit: withdraw whole position now. But idle WETH is 13 — withdrawal of $1,000 WETH (~0.22 WETH) would fail or be partially fillable? 13 WETH idle ≈ $58k at $4,500 ETH. Actually 13 WETH ≈ $58,500. So a $1,000 withdrawal might actually succeed right now (13 WETH idle > 0.22 WETH needed). But idle is "falling" — 122 at 20:00, 13 at 20:05. It could be zero soon. Still, at 20:05 there were 13 WETH idle. A $1,000 position = ~0.22 WETH. It might just barely be possible. But utilization 99.7% with 100-block avg >99% means withdrawals will keep failing as idle goes to zero.

- reduce_to_target / reduce_light: partial withdrawals, same liquidity problem.

Risk level: This is clearly high or critical. The WETH reserve on Aave V3 Core has:
1. Confirmed bad debt (~$236M borrowed against stolen rsETH collateral).
2. Liquidity exhausted (utilization ~100%, idle ~13 WETH) — suppliers cannot withdraw.
3. Bad debt socialization via Umbrella pending — aWETH value may be impaired.
4. Bank-run dynamics: massive withdrawals ongoing.

For a WETH supplier with no debt, the loss is real: the pool's WETH backs the attacker's uncollateralized borrow. The deficit will be covered by Umbrella (safety module) if it has capacity — Umbrella backstop for WETH reserve... Aave's Umbrella slashes safety module staked AAVE/USDT/etc. to cover bad debt. Whether it fully covers $236M is uncertain. The news says "partial withdrawals may only become possible after Umbrella settles the deficit" — implying impairment.

So risk: critical. The position's value is impaired and exit liquidity is gone.

Action: What's the best action? Ideally exit — but can the keeper even execute? The instructions: "you cannot move funds, only propose an action; the corridor limits enforce safety." So we propose exit. Even if withdrawal may fail due to zero liquidity, proposing exit is the right call — attempt to withdraw whatever is possible, queue/withdraw as liquidity allows. Alternatively, hold because exit is impossible? The framework: "Staying put during a real incident can leave funds stuck or lost even when prices look normal." Here funds are already stuck-ish. The action taxonomy: exit = withdraw or unwind the whole position now.

Given bad debt confirmed and the reserve impaired, exit is the right proposal — attempt full withdrawal now while any idle WETH remains (13 WETH idle could cover $1,000). Waiting means competing with a bank run; utilization at 100% means any delay risks permanent inability to withdraw until Umbrella settles (and possibly at a haircut).

Actually, let me think about whether "exit" vs "reduce_to_target". The position is $1,000 WETH supply, no debt. There's no "target" that makes sense other than zero given the reserve is impaired. Exit is correct.

Risk: critical. Reasons:
- Confirmed ~$292M KelpDAO rsETH bridge exploit; stolen rsETH used as collateral on Aave V3 Core to borrow ~52.4k WETH (~$236M) bad debt borne by WETH suppliers (O05, O21, O22).
- WETH reserve liquidity exhausted: utilization ~100%, idle 13 WETH and falling — withdrawals effectively blocked; bank run underway (O13, O14, O17).
